newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Profit-taking, downgrades hit Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking, downgrades hit Brussels bourse.

text.p: A bout of profit-taking, some brokerage downgrades and weaker bonds hit the Brussels bourse on Tuesday, sending the Bel-20 index a third of a percentage lower in early trade while neighbouring markets were firm.
By 0915 the Bel-20 stood 6.78 points lower at 2,373.92.
Chemical group Solvay was among the most active shares, shedding nearly one percent at 21,000 francs as international investors continued to switch to German chemicals.
"Solvay is just not competitive enough vis-a-vis the large German firms. It has also waited to long to diversify into pharmaceuticals," one dealer said.
Solvay's slide, started on June 11, was now at the point where its long-term uptrend was in danger of being broken, one dealer said.

Oil group PetroFina was down 0.92 pct at 13,500 francs, partly because Salomon Brothers said in a report on the oil and gas sector it was negative short term on Petrofina. Salomon said it maintains an underweight on the entire sector, as the fragile one-dollar oil price rally on delayed Iraqi exports is likely to reverse over the next few months.
Salomon estimated Petrofina's 1997 price/earnings at 19.3, which is at the high end of the sector's range in Europe.

Generale Bank was unchanged at 13,850 francs despite a "reduce" recommendation by KB Securities. Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) -- often cited as a candidate for a merger with Generale Bank -- was down one percent at 9,010 francs.
Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere SA (UM) and shipper CMB were among the few shares to buck the down trend. Both are dollar sensitive stocks.
